text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is eyeing Lithuania's privatisation process and is considering an equity stake in Lithuanian Telecom, an official said on Wednesday.
"Obviously the telecom is one of the first on the list, and we've been discussing supporting the telecom company," EBRD Deputy Vice President Guy de Selliers told reporters.
De Selliers also said the EBRD was interested in the Klaipeda Stevedoring Company (KLASCO).
Both companies are on a list of 13 key enterprises slated for privatisation by international tender in the next two years.
The EBRD is already involved with Lithuanian Telecom, having loaned the company $25 million in 1994 for modernisation and infrastructure.

"We have already lent $25 million, but we could look at providing another $30 million to $50 million combination of debt and equity in the short to medium-term in the next few months," de Selliers said.
"I think it's fair to say it's a very valuable company," de Selliers said.
Officials are now in the process of selecting a lead adviser for the privatisation from among 23 applicants.

"The important thing ...is that the controling stake be sold at the largest price possible to a strategic investor who can really help modernise the company and bring it into the 21st Century," de Selliers said.
"And of course, we are not the strategic investor," he said, adding that the EBRD would be a minority investor.
The EBRD has invested in 16 projects in Lithuania, five in the public sector and 11 in the private sector. The projects are worth a total of ECU 162.3 million.
